title: Link-irregular tournaments exist for every order at least six

creators.name: Bhattacharjee, Deep
creators.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India

description:
A digraph is link-irregular if no two of its vertices have isomorphic links. Bastien and Khormali conjectured that a link-irregular tournament on n vertices exists if and only if n ≥ 6, and proved the case n ≤ 8. We prove the conjecture for every n, by a construction that adds two vertices at a time: a vertex beating every old vertex, a vertex beaten by every old vertex, and one arc between them.

The archive contains the paper (PDF, LaTeX sources with the figure as PNG, arXiv tarball) and independent checks in C, C++, Bash, Python, Julia and Lean 4, including an exhaustive count of link-irregular tournaments on up to seven vertices (none up to five, 4 on six, 139 on seven, up to isomorphism). A Lean 4 proof with Mathlib proves the theorem for every n ≥ 6 using only the standard axioms; a second Lean file checks in the kernel that no tournament on 2 to 5 vertices is link-irregular.
